summary.intent: Manage and ship the CipherBox v2.0 milestone via /gsd-manager across multiple sessions: verify Phase 70.1, fix a false 'Executing' status on Phase 69, plan and execute Phases 74/75/77 in the background (with quota-interruption resumption), and run /ship-phase 74 through PR #607, including a deep investigation into a macOS-only desktop-e2e overwrite-rename failure that the user insisted be root-caused and fixed before merge rather than deferred.
summary.outcome: Phases 70.1, 75, and 77 were fully verified/completed; Phase 74 was executed, shipped to PR #607, and — after the user pushed back on an initial 'infra flake' misdiagnosis — a genuine Phase-74 regression (scope-exit rotation not marking rotated folders as locally mutated, letting a stale metadata refresh clobber refreshed keys) was found via 10 local FUSE-T reproductions and fixed in grant_scope.rs, verified deterministic across 3 clean runs, and pushed to the PR; several related defects (SC#2 hex/base64 encoding bug, dirty-resume key surfacing, a Greptile P1 WinFsp guard) were also fixed, and a systemic hex/base64 hardening todo was logged.

repo: Two encoding domains coexist by convention with no type enforcement: internal node-codec/stored sealed refs use base64, share API wire fields (encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey/itemNameEncrypted) use hex — this has caused repeated recurring bugs (captured as a high-severity hardening todo).

GSD's plan-file scanner (plan-scan.cjs:28) has a loose `/PLAN/i` substring fallback that miscounts any .md file containing 'PLAN' (e.g. '...WRITE-PLANE-RESEARCH.md') as a real plan file, causing false 'partial/executing' phase status.

Sub-agents launched at the repo root cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree — the working pattern for background phase work is sequential processing on the main checkout switched per feat branch, not parallel worktrees.

macOS FUSE-T/SMB's overwrite-rename issues an `open()` on the *source* file before renaming; Linux's kernel rename never opens either file. This asymmetry is why rotation races only surface on macOS desktop-e2e and never on Linux CI.

`drain_refresh_completions` (fs.rs) already guards `mutated_folders`/`publish_queue` against a stale metadata refresh clobbering keys via `apply_owned_children`, but scope-exit rotations previously didn't mark their folders as mutated, so they weren't covered by this existing guard.

`write_sealed` AEAD binds `node.generation()` in its AAD (crates/core/src/node/seal.rs ~188-192), so any republish after a generation bump must re-seal the write body at the new generation, not carry the old one forward.

The API's IPNS resolve is read-after-write consistent for normal DB rows (confirmed via instrumentation: 596 `normal`, 0 `seqFloor` in one run) — shared-folder nodes are NOT served from lagging DHT/network state, ruling out API-side eventual consistency as a rotation-race cause.

`apply_owned_children` (crates/fuse/src/inode.rs) re-materializes every File child with `cid: String::new()` on a background metadata refresh, forcing a re-resolve from IPNS even if the file was already locally resolved — a real (separate, filed) durability gap.

All 4 share DTOs (create-share, create-invite, claim-invite, update-grant) validate encryptedReadKey/encryptedWriteKey/itemNameEncrypted as hex via `@Matches(/^(?:[0-9a-fA-F]{2})+$/)` — any client code touching these fields must hex-encode, not base64-encode.

code.finding: Grant re-mint (`re_mint_grants_rooted_at`) was base64-encoding `encrypted_read_key` for the share-grant wire field, but the API requires hex — caused a runtime 400 that broke SC#2 grant re-mint end-to-end; fixed to hex::encode. Internal node-codec fields (read_sealed, read_key_sealed) correctly remain base64.

Root cause of the macOS-only Part D overwrite-rename failure: scope-exit rotation republishes folders via the rotation engine 'out of band' without marking them as `mutated_folders`, so a stale in-flight metadata refresh (resolved pre-rotation, completes post-rotation) can clobber the freshly-refreshed inode keys via apply_owned_children, causing parent/child key divergence and cascading AES-GCM failures on retry. Fix: mark rotated folders as mutated after key refresh so the existing drain_refresh_completions guard protects them.

Rotation republishes rotated nodes with `write_sealed: None` (write-plane preservation explicitly deferred to a Phase-72 follow-up per comment) — causes 'no write_sealed body' errors on subsequent owned-walks and would prevent replay.rs from recovering the signing seed after rotation; real durability bug, prototyped a fix but reverted to keep the Part-D fix minimal, filed as a separate todo instead.

Async FilePointer resolution captures the file's read_key at spawn time; if a rotation republishes the file with a new key before the in-flight resolution completes, the resolution unseals with the stale key and fails. A read-path self-heal (re-resolve with current key) was attempted but proven insufficient since the underlying published data itself could be inconsistent (not just the captured key).

fuser rename path guards source/dest kind compatibility (ENOTDIR/EISDIR) before the non-empty-folder check; the WinFsp handle_rename path lacked this guard, letting file↔directory overwrite-renames slip through (Greptile P1) — ported the guard using new STATUS_NOT_A_DIRECTORY/STATUS_FILE_IS_A_DIRECTORY NTSTATUS helpers in operations.rs.

workflow: When a user challenges a hasty 'infra flake' diagnosis with concrete log evidence, stop and re-investigate empirically rather than defending the initial read — local reproduction on the same OS/filesystem stack is far faster and more conclusive than reasoning from CI logs alone.

Reproducing a flaky platform-specific e2e failure locally requires exactly matching the CI toolchain (e.g. building against FUSE-T's fuse.pc via PKG_CONFIG_PATH override, not the system's macFUSE pkgconfig) or the repro won't trigger the real bug.

Key-fingerprint instrumentation (logging short hashes of keys at publish/unseal/child-ref points) was the technique that finally pinned an intermittent crypto-mismatch race after several plausible-but-wrong fixes failed — cheap temporary debug logging plus multiple full e2e run cycles (~10 min each) was necessary to converge.

Deterministic confirmation (3 consecutive clean runs) was required before trusting a fix for an intermittent-looking failure that had actually been consistent (7/7 prior fails) — a single pass isn't sufficient evidence for a race-condition fix.

Revert exploratory/instrumentation code promptly once it's served its diagnostic purpose, and keep the final fix diff minimal — several plausible fixes (write_sealed preservation, coalesced dest-gate, naive self-heal) were tried, verified insufficient, and cleanly reverted rather than left in as speculative hardening.

Ship-phase pipelines benefit from delegating independent audit gates (secure, crypto-privacy review, security-review, simplify) to a single sub-agent run in parallel with the orchestrator holding the SDK-E2E gate for exclusive stack access, avoiding build/stack contention.

When background agents may hit an API quota/session limit, verify actual on-disk state (git log, plan files, branch names) rather than trusting agent-reported status — notifications can undersell real progress (e.g. planners reported as 'failed' had actually committed research/patterns) or overstate it.

friction: GSD's plan-scanner false-positive (substring match on 'PLAN') caused a real phase to show as falsely 'Executing', requiring multi-step investigation before the true root cause (not the initial UAT-stub guess) was found.

Sub-agents cannot EnterWorktree into a pre-existing worktree, which broke the initial background-planning parallelization strategy and forced a pivot to sequential main-checkout-per-branch processing mid-session.
Hit the session/API quota limit three separate times mid-autonomous-run, requiring CronCreate-based scheduled resumes and manual state reassessment each time.
One resume agent used a flawed self-made background-wait loop and stalled for ~21 minutes without making progress, requiring a relaunch with explicit 'no background-wait' instructions.
The gsd commit helper intermittently false-negatives `commit_failed` while the commit actually lands, requiring manual `git log` verification instead of blind retries.

Root-causing the macOS overwrite-rename bug required 10 full local reproduction cycles (~10 min each, full docker stack reset + rebuild + mount) after three earlier hypothesis-driven fixes (write_sealed preservation, read-path self-heal, coalesced dest-gate) each proved insufficient or misdirected.

CodeRabbit's PR-level web review surfaced significantly more findings (12 unresolved threads, including a Greptile P1 security issue) than its local CLI review (8, all doc-only), requiring a second triage pass after the PR was already believed ready.

`ts-rotatednodes-defensive-copy-parity` todo remains open — the TS engine's root/child commit branches (engine.ts:2064/:2235) still lack the defensive Uint8Array copy that Rust's `.clone()` provides.

Server-side DTO doc-comment mislabels ('Hex-encoded' on base64 fields in apps/api/src/shares/dto/share-response.dto.ts) still need fixing but require OpenAPI codegen + regenerated client commit, deferred as out-of-phase-scope.
